cards.rationale: Heparin is monitored with aPTT; protamine sulfate reverses it.
Warfarin is monitored with PT/INR; vitamin K reverses it.
Hold digoxin for an apical pulse < 60; low potassium worsens toxicity.
Loop/thiazide diuretics lose potassium; spironolactone keeps it.
Beta-blockers slow heart rate; never stop them abruptly (rebound).
A respiratory rate < 12 after an opioid is the red flag.
Reverses benzo sedation/respiratory depression; use cautiously (seizure risk).
Protects the liver; most effective given early after overdose.
Watch respirations ≥12, present DTRs, and urine output ≥30 mL/hr.
Narrow range; dehydration or low sodium raises the level toward toxicity.
Both high and low potassium cause life-threatening dysrhythmias.
Sodium drives fluid balance and neuro status.
Above 2.0 → toxicity; check potassium alongside it.
Too high = bleeding; too low = clot risk.
aPTT monitors heparin; PT/INR monitors warfarin.
Below 70 = hypoglycemia (treat fast carbs); high = hyperglycemia.
Best single marker of kidney function; rises as function drops.
Below 50k sharply raises bleeding risk; below 20k = spontaneous bleeding.

cards.front: Potassium 6.8 — what and what do you see?
cards.back: Hyperkalemia → tall, peaked T waves; cardiac emergency
cards.rationale: Calcium protects the heart; insulin+D50 shifts K into cells; dialysis removes it.
Low pH + high CO₂ = hypoventilation (COPD, sedation).

cards.back: Measles, TB, Varicella (chickenpox) — N95 + negative-pressure room
cards.rationale: Contact = C. diff/MRSA; Droplet = flu/meningitis/pertussis.

cards.back: Contact precautions; wash with soap and water (not alcohol gel)
cards.rationale: Alcohol doesn’t kill C. diff spores — friction with soap removes them.
Then acute-over-chronic and unstable-over-stable.
To use an extinguisher: PASS (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep).

cards.front: What can you delegate to a UAP?
cards.back: Stable, routine tasks: vitals, hygiene, feeding, ambulating, I&O
cards.rationale: The RN keeps Assess, Teach, Evaluate, and nursing judgment/meds.
cards.hint: If it needs a nurse’s brain, it stays with the nurse.

cards.front: Gold standard to confirm NG tube placement?
cards.rationale: The air/auscultation test is unreliable; gastric aspirate pH ≤5 supports placement.
cards.hint: When in doubt, X-ray it out.

cards.front: Two ways to break a sterile field?
cards.back: Reaching across it, or letting it get wet; the outer 1-inch border is contaminated
cards.rationale: Keep it above the waist and in sight; when in doubt, throw it out.
cards.hint: Below the waist or out of sight isn’t sterile.

cards.back: Least restrictive: bed low, call light in reach, nonslip footwear, frequent rounding
cards.rationale: Restraints and 4 side rails are last resort (they ARE restraints).
